title: AI as Normal Technology
subtitle: An alternative to the vision of AI as a potential superintelligence
publisher: Knight First Amendment Institute at Columbia University
pitch: The authors of AI Snake Oil argue AI will be transformative but normal, like electricity: adoption takes decades, and humans stay in control through ordinary institutions.

chapters.t: Part I: The Speed of Progress
chapters.g: Invention is fast but diffusion into society is slow, held back by safety, regulation and the need to change how work is done.

chapters.t: Part II: What a World With Advanced AI Might Look Like
chapters.g: Humans will mostly do the work of controlling and specifying AI, not be replaced.
Accidents, arms races, misuse and misalignment look different through the normal technology lens.
Favouring resilience over non-proliferation, and reducing uncertainty instead of acting on speculation.
Why the worldview you start with shapes every conclusion about AI.

ideas: AI's impact will unfold over decades, not months.
Diffusion, not invention, sets the pace.
Control stays with humans through institutions.
Resilience beats trying to stop AI from spreading.

args.a: AI will be a normal, slow moving transformative technology.
args.c: Those worried about an intelligence explosion say AI improving AI could break the pattern of slow diffusion.

args.a: Non-proliferation policies do more harm than good.
args.c: Others argue some capabilities, like bioweapon help, must be restricted.

questions: Is AI more like electricity or more like nuclear weapons?
What slows AI adoption where you live?
Which worldview do you start from, and why?

quiz.q: What do the authors compare AI to?
o: Other general purpose technologies like electricity

quiz.q: What sets the pace of impact, in their view?
What earlier book did they write?
